title: Desk Guidance: Recomputed Patient Payment Plan Installment Over the Remaining Schedule
content:
**Remaining schedule.** On a signed **Patient Payment Plan** whose installment is recomputed after added balances, the remaining schedule is the plan's current number of scheduled installments extended by the tier's add-on term extension, never beyond the longest recomputed schedule, which is the tier's maximum term; less the installments already paid, counted as the installment payment entries numbered 1 or more; and less the missed installments the plan records, which stay due apart from the schedule. The remaining schedule is at least one installment.

**New installment.** The new installment is the plan balance divided by that remaining schedule, rounded half-up to the cent, never below the recompute floor, which is the tier's minimum monthly payment.

**Order.** The extended schedule is settled first, the longest recomputed schedule is applied to it next, the installments already paid and the missed installments are taken away after that (leaving at least one installment), and the recompute floor is applied last to the divided figure.

### Worked example (hypothetical figures)

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Current scheduled installments | 24 |
| Tier add-on term extension | 6 months, giving 30 |
| Tier maximum term | 36 (30 is within it) |
| Installment payment entries numbered 1 or more | 10 |
| Missed installments recorded | 0 |
| Remaining schedule | 30 less 10 less 0, so 20 |
| Plan balance | 3000.00 |
| Divided figure | 3000.00 divided by 20, 150.00 |
| Tier minimum monthly payment | 100.00 |
| New installment | 150.00 |

Had the plan balance been 1500.00, the divided figure of 75.00 would sit below the 100.00 floor and the new installment would be 100.00.
